item.title: SMART SDK and AgentCore Simplify WhatsApp Agent Deployment on AWS
item.description:
SMART SDK and AgentCore Simplify WhatsApp Agent Deployment on AWS

Across Latin America, India, and Southeast Asia, WhatsApp is one of the most widely used messaging applications, but building a robust agent on top of it requires handling complex, type-dependent payloads, media processing pipelines, and strict compliance rules. To simplify this process, SMART (Social Messaging Agent Runtime Toolkit) is available as an open source Python SDK and Terraform stack that provides the full channel layer for agents running on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.

🧩 How it works

SMART allows you to provide an agent that runs on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime, and it handles the underlying channel logic. The architecture utilizes the following services:

  • AWS End User Messaging Social: Receives inbound WhatsApp messages and routes them to the processing layer.
  • AWS Lambda: Handles the channel logic, including verifying SNS message signatures, normalizing payloads, and rate-limiting users (20 messages per minute by default).
  • Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: Provides the runtime, memory, and observability for the agent.
  • Supporting Services: Amazon DynamoDB (optional, for per-user state), AWS Secrets Manager, Amazon CloudWatch, and Amazon S3 supply state management, credentials, monitoring, and storage.

The AgentCore runtime hosts and scales the agent without requiring infrastructure management. AgentCore memory persists conversation history across sessions and deployments, scoped automatically to each phone number. The create_session_manager() function binds the agent to this memory, with a default retention period of 7 days. Frameworks such as Strands Agents get memory wired automatically, while LangGraph and Pydantic-AI can integrate with the conversation loop.

⚙️ Key details

Wiring up a custom WhatsApp agent typically involves configuring more than 10 AWS services and learning specific system behaviors. SMART abstracts these complexities, including:

  • Inbound message authentication and normalization.
  • Processing pipelines for media such as voice notes, images, and documents.
  • Durable schedules for reminders and authenticated paths for external systems to trigger outbound messages.
  • Compliance with Meta’s requirement that messages sent more than 24 hours after the user’s last message must use pre-approved templates.
  • Handling of intermediate tool outputs (like button lists or progress updates) to prevent conversation history corruption.

🚀 Availability

SMART is an open source solution. A single command deploys the entire infrastructure to your AWS account. Webmotors, originally scoped as a two-month engagement, compressed delivery to six weeks and moved their internal team into controlled production ahead of a full launch using this approach.

Source: Build WhatsApp AI agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services

item.title: AI Assistant for WhatsApp Ordering Powered by Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Nova Models
item.description:
AI Assistant for WhatsApp Ordering Powered by Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Nova Models

A new end-to-end AI ordering assistant has been developed for WhatsApp, utilizing Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Amazon Nova models to manage customer interactions. The system allows users to place restaurant orders from greeting to confirmation through a single WhatsApp Business number.

🔍 Overview

Customers can interact with the assistant using three distinct channels that share one backend and cross-channel memory:

  • Text messages
  • Voice notes
  • Voice calls

The solution uses the Meta WhatsApp Business Platform as the customer front door, which reaches more than two billion people. Because of the shared memory system, a customer who texts one day and calls the next is recognized as the same person.

🧩 How it works

Component Role in the System
Meta WhatsApp Business Platform Acts as the front door, exposing the Cloud API, Messages API, Media API, and Calling API.
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Hosts the AI agents and manages cross-channel memory and gateway functions.
Amazon Nova 2 Lite Processes text through the Amazon Bedrock Converse API.
Amazon Nova 2 Sonic Handles real-time speech for both voice notes and calls.
AgentCore Gateway A managed MCP server that exposes the backend REST API as tools for agents.
AgentCore Memory A shared record keyed by hashed customer ID to maintain state across channels.
Model Context Protocol (MCP) Enables agents to reach the restaurant backend.
Amazon SQS Provides an inbound queue to decouple quick acknowledgment from asynchronous processing.
AWS Lambda Runs the webhook ingest, worker, message sender, and ordering logic.

⚙️ Key details

The infrastructure is deployed and managed with specific architectural controls:

  • Deployment: The AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) provisions the AWS side of the solution and emits the webhook URL for Meta registration.
  • Processing: Inbound traffic arrives at a single HTTPS webhook provided by Amazon API Gateway. It is acknowledged immediately with a 200 status and processed asynchronously so no request blocks the response.
  • Security and Isolation: Each conversation runs in its own microVM within the AgentCore runtime to keep sessions isolated.
  • API Architecture: The system uses two REST APIs. The first is a public, regional HTTPS webhook. The second is an IAM-authorized backend API that sits in front of the ordering business logic.

#AWS #AmazonBedrock #WhatsApp #AIagents #AmazonNova

Source: Deploy a multimodal WhatsApp ordering assistant with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
